livinghorizon.options.title: Living Horizon
livinghorizon.options.enabled.tooltip: Draw other players past the range where the server stops sending them. The toggle key flips this too.
livinghorizon.options.showVehicles.toolt: Draw the horse, boat or happy ghast a distant player was last seen riding.
livinghorizon.options.offlinePose.toolti: How a player who logged off is shown where they were last.
livinghorizon.options.lostTimeoutSeconds: Without the data pack: how long a player stays where they were once the locator bar loses them (sneaking, another dimension).
livinghorizon.options.glowOutline.toolti: A glowing outline around distant players and mobs, seen through terrain.
livinghorizon.options.renderTrackedVehic: The game hides small entities early: a friend in a boat would float on nothing. Keeps a mount carrying a player drawn.
livinghorizon.options.distantMobs.toolti: Animals, villagers and golems stay visible once out of range, where they were, strolling around, looking around and grazing. No AI.
livinghorizon.options.maxDistantMobs.too: How many remembered mobs are drawn at once: the nearest ones. Lower it if the game slows down. Warning: unlimited here and in Mob distance together can crash the game.
livinghorizon.options.mobMaxDistance.too: How far away distant mobs are drawn, in blocks. Past it they are hidden. Unlimited draws them as far as they are remembered. Warning: unlimited here and in Mobs drawn at most together can crash the game.
How far away distant players are drawn, in blocks. Past it they are hidden.
livinghorizon.options.depthOcclusion.too: Distant mobs and players are hidden by Voxy or Distant Horizons terrain pixel by pixel, like behind any block: half behind a tree, half visible. Needed with Distant Horizons, and with shader packs such as Photon, which keep Voxy out of the depth buffer.
livinghorizon.options.extendFarPlane.too: The game clips everything past four times the render distance. On: pushed back to the farthest player. Off: those are drawn closer and smaller, and show through terrain.
Above 0, a distant player or mob is never drawn smaller than this many pixels, and so looks bigger than it is far away.
livinghorizon.status.none: No other player is being followed.
livinghorizon.status.pack.on: Data pack: running, positions are exact.
livinghorizon.status.pack.off: Data pack: not found, positions come from the locator bar.
livinghorizon.status.cost: Cost: %s ms per tick, %s ms per frame; %s puppets drawn, %s skipped (behind you or too small).
livinghorizon.lod.missing: Neither Voxy nor Distant Horizons is installed: nothing to hide behind.
livinghorizon.lod.depth: Far terrain depth on distant mobs: %s.
livinghorizon.lod.probe.hit: Looking ahead, the first block %s knows is %s blocks away.
livinghorizon.lod.probe.none: Looking ahead, %s knows no block within 4096 blocks.
A mob with a name tag is remembered and shown whatever its type.
livinghorizon.options.chooseMobs.tooltip: Which mobs and boats are shown far away, one by one.
livinghorizon.options.forgetMobs.tooltip: Forgets every remembered mob on this server. The data pack's come back by themselves.
livinghorizon.options.forgetMobs.confirm: Every mob remembered on this server is forgotten. Mobs published by the data pack will come back; the others only once met again.
livinghorizon.options.scanMobs.tooltip: Reads the mobs of the chunks around you from the world itself, no need to walk there: they appear on the horizon at once. Mobs remembered there and no longer found are forgotten.
livinghorizon.options.scanMobs.unavailab: Only in a single player world, once in it: a server never sends the mobs of chunks far from you. On a server, the data pack shares them.
livinghorizon.options.scanRadius.tooltip: How many chunks around you a scan reads (16 blocks each). Also /livinghorizon scan <radius>, which takes any radius.
livinghorizon.scan.started: Reading the mobs of the chunks within %s chunks...
livinghorizon.scan.done: Scan done: %s mobs found within %s chunks.
livinghorizon.scan.failed: The scan failed: see the log.
livinghorizon.scan.unavailable: Scanning only works in a single player world: a server never sends the mobs of chunks far from you. On a server, the data pack shares them.
livinghorizon.options.restoreDefaults.to: Puts every setting back to its default, the chosen mobs and birds included.
livinghorizon.options.restoreDefaults.co: Every Living Horizon setting goes back to its default, including the mobs and birds you chose. Remembered mobs are kept.
livinghorizon.options.forgetSleepers.too: Removes every player shown asleep where they logged off, on this server.
livinghorizon.options.forgetSleepers.con: Every player shown asleep on this server disappears. With the data pack, they come back from their last position.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.title: Mobs and boats shown far away
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.shared.to: %s - ★ published by the data pack: shown even if you never met it. Animated: strolls around. Still: stays where it was.
livinghorizon.options.mobTypes.local.too: %s - not in the data pack: shown only where you met it yourself. Animated: strolls around. Still: stays where it was.
livinghorizon.options.skyBirds.tooltip: Birds and bats around you: flocks, birds of prey, gulls, pigeons, robins, tits, bats at night. Only on your screen.
livinghorizon.options.birdMaxDistance.to: How far away birds can be, in blocks. Far birds are a few pixels, like real ones.
livinghorizon.options.birdDensity.toolti: How many birds, all kinds together: 100 is the usual, 200 twice as many, 0 none.
livinghorizon.options.birdMinHeight.tool: Blocks above you, or the sea when it is higher, below which flocks and birds of prey never fly.
livinghorizon.options.chooseBirds.toolti: Which kinds of birds there are, one by one.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.title: Birds
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.flocks.t: Clouds of small birds crossing the sky, far away.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.geese.to: Large birds flying high in a V.
Large birds circling a spot, gliding, drifting with the wind.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.gulls.to: White birds low over beaches and the sea; now and then one lands on the beach, and takes off if you come close.
Sitting on the top of tall buildings; they take off when you come close and land again later.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.robins.t: Hopping and pecking in fields of crops; they fly off when you come close.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.tits.too: Flitting about the tops of trees.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.ducks.to: On lakes, rivers and ponds; now and then they fly to another spot. They never let you come near.
livinghorizon.options.birdTypes.bats.too: At night, flitting around the scenery, or hanging upside down under leaves and roofs near you until you come close. They go home at dawn.
Now and then a flock of the game's parrots.
livinghorizon.options.ufo.tooltip: An easter egg: now and then, far away, a flying saucer comes for a cow. Only on your screen. /livinghorizon ufo calls it now.
livinghorizon.options.birdSize.tooltip: How much bigger than life the birds are drawn. 1 is true to life.
livinghorizon.options.hideOccludedMobs.t: Distant mobs the terrain hides entirely (the far terrain included) are not drawn at all, instead of drawn and covered pixel by pixel. Cheaper with many mobs. Decided from the depth of the picture: a mob even partly in view is still drawn, and one shows up a frame or two after the view clears.
livinghorizon.options.impostors.tooltip: Far enough away, a distant player or mob is drawn as a flat picture of itself, turned to you, instead of its whole model. The pictures are baked from the game's own models when you join a world and when resource packs change, so skins and packs are followed. Much cheaper with many mobs.
livinghorizon.options.impostorDistance.t: Blocks: past this distance, impostors stand in for the models. Lower is cheaper; higher keeps the full models longer.
livinghorizon.options.debug.tooltip: The far plane, the glowing outline, boxes and labels on distant mobs, a panel of counts and costs, the depth buffer with the far terrain, and a switch for every optimisation.
livinghorizon.options.impostorPreview.to: What the impostors look like, and a button to bake them again.
livinghorizon.options.debugHud.tooltip: Top left. In the F3 screen, turn on "living_horizon" in the debug options (F3 + F6): cost per tick and frame, what became of every distant mob in the last frame, far terrain reads and depth, how far this server sends mobs, which optimisations are on.
livinghorizon.options.debugBoxes.tooltip: A box and a dot around every distant mob and player, seen through terrain, in the colour of what became of it: green copy drawn, cyan real mob drawn by the mod, blue player, yellow too small, orange behind blocks, red outside the view, purple being built, grey past the maximum.
livinghorizon.options.debugLabels.toolti: Over each box: what became of it, its kind, its distance and its size on screen in pixels.
livinghorizon.options.debugGameMobs.tool: White boxes around the mobs the game draws itself, to see where the mod takes over.
livinghorizon.options.debugOutlines.tool: How each distant figure is drawn, seen through terrain: a green outline around the 3D copies, a magenta one around impostors, and an orange cross where a mob is not drawn at all (behind blocks, too small, outside the view, waiting). The cross only says where, not what.
livinghorizon.options.debugDepthView.too: The depth buffer in the bottom right corner, near white to far black, the sky in blue.
livinghorizon.options.optViewCulling.too: Copies behind you or to the side are not prepared at all.
livinghorizon.options.optTinyCulling.too: Copies smaller than about half a pixel are not prepared (only at true size, minimum size 0).
livinghorizon.options.optLazyDepth.toolt: The far terrain's depth (Voxy or Distant Horizons) is merged only on frames that draw something past the render distance. Off: every frame.
livinghorizon.options.optParallelRead.to: The far world (Voxy or Distant Horizons) is read on several threads at once. Off: one thread.
livinghorizon.options.optColumnCache.too: Ground already read in the far world is kept two minutes. Off: read again every time.
livinghorizon.options.optOcclusionQuerie: How "Skip mobs behind blocks" decides, which must be on: the GPU tests each mob's box against the depth of the picture - what you see, Voxy or Distant Horizons included - and a mob with not one pixel in view is not drawn. Off, to compare: lines of sight are traced in the far terrain's world instead, which needs Voxy or Distant Horizons.
livinghorizon.options.optStillTiny.toolt: A distant mob only a few pixels high on screen slides and turns without playing its walking and idle animations, which could not be seen. Off: always animated.
livinghorizon.options.optBackgroundBuild: Saved mobs are read off the game's thread and built within 2 ms per tick. Off: all at once, on the game's thread.
livinghorizon.debug.on: Living Horizon debug: on (panel and boxes).
livinghorizon.debug.hud.title: Living Horizon - debug
livinghorizon.debug.hud.mobs: Mobs: %s remembered, %s chosen, %s built, %s waiting, %s sent by the server
livinghorizon.debug.hud.depth: Far terrain depth: %s; merged last frame: %s
livinghorizon.debug.hud.reads: Far terrain reads: %s threads, %s tasks pending, %s columns known
livinghorizon.debug.f3.polygons: Living Horizon: %s polygons (%s triangles) - %s full models, %s polygons; %s impostors
livinghorizon.debug.f3.impostors: Living Horizon impostors: %s sheets baked, %s waiting
livinghorizon.debug.f3.impostorsFailed: Living Horizon impostors: baking failed, full models are used (see the log)
livinghorizon.impostors.title: Impostors
livinghorizon.impostors.off: Impostors are off: switch them on in the settings to bake and use them.
livinghorizon.impostors.empty: Nothing baked yet: the distant players and mobs on hand are baked within a few seconds.
livinghorizon.impostors.regenerate.toolt: Throws every picture away and bakes the figures on hand again, even after a failed bake.
livinghorizon.debug.opt.lazy: far terrain depth only when needed
